ticker: Three workers die at Tata iPhone parts factory in Tamil Nadu
Pentagon chief Hegseth calls impeachment moves a farce
US State Department serves India summons in Pannun lawsuit
China's trade surplus tops $1 trillion for second consecutive year
US-mediated Russia-Ukraine peace talks begin in Abu Dhabi

articles.headline: Three Workers Die at Tata iPhone Parts Factory
articles.brief: Three contract workers tragically died from gas inhalation while inspecting a tank at Tata Electronics’ iPhone components factory in Tamil Nadu. Both Apple and Tata have launched full investigations into the safety incident, while subcontractor Nalco Water pledged complete cooperation with local authorities.

articles.headline: Pentagon Chief Hegseth Defends Actions Amid Impeachment Push
articles.brief: US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth dismissed efforts to impeach him over lawful military operations in Iran as a farce destined to fail. Speaking at a press conference following the introduction of eight articles of impeachment by Representative Thomas Massie, Hegseth defended his record.

articles.headline: US State Department Serves India Summons in Pannun Lawsuit
articles.brief: The US State Department has formally served India with summonses in a civil lawsuit filed by Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun. The lawsuit involves an alleged failed assassination plot investigated by US authorities, though the State Department clarified it takes no position on the case.

articles.headline: China Trade Surplus Tops $1 Trillion For Second Year
articles.brief: China's trade surplus surpassed $1 trillion in the first ten months of the year, powered by a massive 35.2% jump in October exports. High-tech goods and AI-related hardware drove the surge, though Beijing continues to face mounting trade tensions with the United States and European Union.

articles.headline: US-Mediated Russia-Ukraine Peace Talks Begin in Abu Dhabi
articles.brief: New diplomatic efforts to end the prolonged conflict have commenced as US-mediated peace talks between Russian and Ukrainian representatives opened in Abu Dhabi. Meanwhile, Ukrainian leadership continues to express skepticism over territorial concessions for peace.

articles.headline: FDA Flags Potential Vision Loss Risk From Weight-Loss Drugs
articles.brief: An extensive FDA analysis of numerous clinical trials involving GLP-1 weight-loss medications has indicated a higher incidence of non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy. Users of these popular diabetes and anti-obesity drugs are advised to remain vigilant about potential vision risks.

articles.headline: Microsoft Presses Trump to Scuttle Chinese Data Center Ban
articles.brief: Tech giant Microsoft is reportedly lobbying the Trump administration to scrap an anticipated ban on Chinese data center technology. The intervention highlights intense corporate concerns over supply chains and regulatory roadblocks facing infrastructure investments.

articles.headline: India Unveils Massive Push for Grid-Scale Energy Storage
articles.brief: The Indian government has launched a substantial funding initiative to deploy 92 GWh of grid-scale energy storage, including pumped hydro and battery systems. The project aims to integrate rising renewable energy capacity, stabilize the electrical grid, and minimize regional power outages.

articles.headline: India Highlights Climate Finance Obligations at Global Forum
articles.brief: During international climate discussions, India urged developed economies to honor their financial commitments to help developing nations adapt to rising environmental hazards. New Delhi emphasized that a fair and rapid transition to cleaner energy requires substantial international support.

articles.headline: India Unemployment Rate Falls to 5.1% in Recent Quarter
articles.brief: Official macroeconomic data reveals that India's unemployment rate dropped to 5.1% during the July-September quarter. The improvement was largely driven by a significant contraction in rural joblessness as agricultural and localized labor markets strengthened.

articles.headline: Nvidia CEO's Alleged Ties to China Chip Shipments Scrutinized
articles.brief: Recent investigative reports suggest that personal ties involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang intersected with substantial high-end microchip shipments to China. The revelations have intensified scrutiny from regulators tracking semiconductor export controls.

articles.headline: India Criticizes US Court Summons Over Pannun Case
articles.brief: New Delhi forcefully rejected a US court order involving top Indian security officials in the Pannun legal dispute, labeling the move a malicious and fabricated attack. Ministry of External Affairs officials condemned the proceedings as legally baseless.

articles.headline: India Uncertified Allied Health Workers Given Path to Register
articles.brief: Draft regulations released under the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions offer a four-year transition window. Uncertified lab technicians and radiographers can now formalize their credentials or face restrictions on future practice.

articles.headline: Blackstone Acquires Stake in IIFL Finance in Capital Boost
articles.brief: Global investment firm Blackstone has injected substantial capital into IIFL Finance, acquiring a major equity stake to bolster the non-banking financial company's balance sheet amid shifting market conditions.
